summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first, which is correct. It then treated the brief as a bounded change. It asked one question, gave a "short design" in chat, and started implementing once I approved. It never wrote a spec document, and no docs/ directory exists. The criteria require this brief to be escalated to the architectural path, so the run fails.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent took the bounded path, gave its design in chat, wrote no spec file under docs/, and started implementing as soon as I approved. Criteria 1 and 5 pass.

observations.description: Router misclassification: changing the login() signature changes a public interface. The agent even noticed a cross-cutting issue: userId has no source on the page and is "caller-asserted", and the server should eventually be the source of truth. It still took the bounded/short-design path and never wrote a spec.
The agent never stated a classification. It just went to "Here's the short design", so a reviewer has to work out which path the router chose.

The agent's first question made a good point: it recommended keeping login(username, password) and taking userId from the server response. Once I chose the literal parameter option, it dropped that concern without reconsidering scope. The client-supplied userId is untrusted, and the agent only flagged that after implementing.

Startup friction in the harness: the folder-trust dialog defaults to "No, exit". A "Newer Opus model available" prompt said the current model was Opus 5, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I picked No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.
The agent checked its change by running app.js in Node against a fake DOM written to /tmp/verify_login.js, outside the repo. It said clearly that it had not tested in a real browser.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The app.js and index.html edits came after it.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: The agent said "OK, we'll add the parameter. Here's the short design:" and put the design only in chat. Running `ls coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". Before I approved, `git status` showed "nothing to commit, working tree clean". No tool call in the session log writes a spec file.

criteria.criterion: Spec doc presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec doc ever existed. What I approved was the in-chat design, which ended "Should I go ahead with this, and should userId be required or optional?" After that the agent edited app.js with a python3 Bash command and updated index.html (+1 -0).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip spec
criteria.evidence: It never said the word "bounded". Every other step matches the bounded path: a short design in chat ("Here's the short design"), no spec file, then implementation straight after "looks good, go ahead". The only "bounded" hits in the session log come from the loaded skill text, not from the agent's own messages.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The agent did not offer a probe plan or anything labeled throwaway. It gave a feature design and then implemented it.
